title: Dependability Orchestration Field Protocol — 90d Playbook
content:
PURPOSE
This is a field-oriented playbook for orchestration of dependability improvements across product, infra, and customer-facing teams. The goal is to create a repeatable 90-day program that moves a service from ad-hoc reliability fixes to SLO-backed operational maturity. This doc is intentionally pragmatic: checklists, ownership agreements, simple runbooks, and a fast feedback loop for rollouts.

BACKGROUND / PROBLEM STATEMENT
- Multiple services report intermittent latency spikes and cache-thrashing under synthetic traffic.
- We lack a consistent SLO onboarding path for smaller feature teams (hand-offs are manual, expectations fuzzy).
- Observability gaps: missing end-to-end traces for the API proxy, tokenized cost per request signal not surfaced to owners.
- On-call contracts are localized; escalation surfaces are inconsistent across feature teams.

OBJECTIVES (90 days)
1) Establish service-level SLOs for 6 pilot services (error-rate and p95 latency) and instrument end-to-end traces.
2) Define on-call contract template and pairing rotation for feature teams + platform SRE.
3) Close top 5 observability gaps that block confident SLO measurement.
4) Run two canary rollouts with automatic fallback and measure degradation impact.
5) Hand off a reproducible onboarding kit and checklist for the next 12 teams.

SUCCESS METRICS (how we’ll know we succeeded)
- 6 pilot services with active SLO dashboards and alerting in place.
- Mean time to detect (MTTD) for pilot services improves by >= 30% vs baseline.
- Canary rollback rate <= 10% (i.e., most canaries succeed without manual intervention after fixes).
- Observability gaps: at least 5 signals fully instrumented (trace id propagation, request-cost, queue depth, backend-saturation, KV cache hit ratio).
- Two post-mortems run for canary incidents with documented follow-ups and assigned owners.

SCOPE / NON-SCOPE
- In scope: API latency/error SLOs, telemetry plumbing, on-call contract for feature teams, canary rollout mechanism, 6 pilot services.
- Out of scope: full platform quota/costing redesign, private deployment (on-prem) integration, model-level quality SLOs (these live with the Applied ML team).

STAKEHOLDERS & ROLES
- Program lead: Aisha Patel (SRE) — overall delivery, exec updates, program decisions.
- Platform Integration: Daniel Kim (Platform Eng) — canary routing, default fallback policy.
- Observability: Ruth Alvarez (Observability) — metrics/trace dashboards, alert tuning.
- Service owners: listed per pilot (Tom Becker, Maya Singh, plus product leads) — implement instrumentation, accept SLOs.
- Solutions Eng / CS liaison: Priya Nair — helps coordinate customer-impact scenarios and runbooks.
- Release & Risk: Release Eng on-call — coordinates cutover windows and blast-radius controls.

90-DAY TIMELINE (high-level weeks)
Weeks 0–2: Kickoff + Discovery
- Stakeholder kickoff, map pilot services, capture current telemetry gaps.
- Run a 1-week baseline collection (synthetic + production sampling).
- Deliverable: baseline dashboard + risk register.

Weeks 3–5: Instrumentation & Minimal Viable SLOs
- Implement trace-id propagation and request-cost metric on pilot services.
- Create SLO draft (objective, measurement window, burn rate).
- Instrument simple alert on burn-rate > 2x for 15m.
- Deliverable: SLO definitions and wired dashboards.

Weeks 6–9: Canary Policy + On-call Contracts
- Define canary policy (traffic percentage ramp, rollback triggers, abort conditions).
- Publish on-call contract template: primary owner, escalation path, paging expectations, pair-on-call schedule.
- Run first canary on a low-traffic service; capture signals and iterate.
- Deliverable: canary policy doc + contract signed by pilot owners.

Weeks 10–12: Full Stretch + Handoff
- Run second canary on a more critical service with guardrails.
- Triage any regressions, update runbooks and postmortems.
- Produce onboarding kit (checklist, Confluence template, automation scripts).
- Deliverable: repeatable onboarding kit and handoff meeting to product platform teams.

DETAILED DELIVERABLES (quick checklist)
- Baseline report: throughput, error-rate, p95/p99 latency for each pilot.
- SLO config files (json/yaml) for each service + one-liner SLO statement.
- Observability fixes: trace propagation PRs, metric exporters, dashboards.
- Canary policy + automation runbook (traffic ramp scripts).
- On-call contract template and rotational calendar.
- Postmortem template and RCA playbook.
- Handoff playbook: 10-step onboarding checklist for new service.

ON-CALL CONTRACT (template highlights)
- Primary owner: product/service owner must be reachable during rollout windows.
- Pager escalation: SRE -> feature owner -> engineering manager -> product.
- Response time expectations: acknowledge page within 15 minutes; initial mitigation plan within 60 minutes.
- Ownership of fixes: feature team owns code fixes, platform SRE supports mitigations and rollback.

OBSERVABILITY & TELEMETRY ACTIVITIES
- Mandatory signals to enable SLOs: request start/end timestamps, error boolean or code, trace-id, upstream service tags, tokenized-cost-per-request.
- Short-term: add span-level sampling on 1% of traffic for heavy services.
- Medium-term: instrument KV cache hit ratio and expose via exporter.
- Dashboards: SLO burn, latency distribution, top N callers by latency, cache hit trend, cost-per-request trend.

INCIDENT RUNBOOK (minimal)
1) Detect: SLO burn alert fires -> runbook link opened.
2) Triage: check canary vs prod, trace waterfall, identify backend saturation or infra flapping.
3) Mitigate: roll traffic back to previous revision OR enable degraded mode (e.g., relax non-critical features).
4) Communicate: post to incident channel with short summary + page + customer-impact note.
5) Postmortem: within 3 business days, assign RCA owner and mitigation owner.

COMMUNICATIONS & CADENCE
- Weekly sync: 30-min working sync every Tuesday with pilot owners, platform, and observability.
- Bi-weekly exec check-in: 30-min with Eng Director for status/risks.
- Slack channel: #dep-orch-90d (use for updates + quick blockers).
- Monthly town hall demo: show dashboards and a canary recap.

RISKS & MITIGATIONS
- Risk: Instrumentation PRs get delayed by feature sprints.
  Mitigation: provide engineering hours from platform pool for instrumentation work.
- Risk: Canary rollback triggers noisy false positives.
  Mitigation: tune alert thresholds; use graduated ramp with short hold windows.
- Risk: Pager fatigue for small teams.
  Mitigation: limit guaranteed hours (block scheduling) and provide pairing with platform SRE.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs (work-in-progress)
- What is the canonical SLO window for short-lived services? 1h or 24h? Need product input.
- Who signs the on-call contract for infra-owned libraries? (platform or feature team?)
- Automation: can we add the SLO config to infra-as-code for seamless promotion? (#TODO: Daniel to prototype)
- Identify 2–3 low-risk customer-impact scenarios to simulate during canary. (Priya to coordinate)

NEXT STEPS (immediate)
- Aisha: schedule pilot kickoff this week and send invite to stakeholders.
- Observability: Ruth to publish baseline dashboard by EOD next Wednesday.
- Platform: Daniel to draft canary policy PR and share for review.
- Service owners: Tom/Maya to prioritize instrumentation tickets in next sprint.

QUICK REFERENCES / LINKS
- SRE handbook: CONFLUENCE-DEP-ORCH-001
- Canary policy draft: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-playbooks/pull/88
- SLO config schema: JIRA-SRE-412 (linked design doc)

NOTES TO SELF (informal)
- Keep checklist small — aim for 8–10 concrete items.
- Expect friction at the telemetry level; plan for 2-day shock absorbers in the timeline.
- This doc will be the seed for a templated Confluence page and a short slide deck for execs.

REVISION HISTORY
- 2026-03-05: Initial draft (Aisha).
- 2026-03-09: Added instrumentation checklist and SLO success metrics (Ruth).
- 2026-03-12: Updated canary cadence and on-call contract template (Daniel).

[END OF PLAYBOOK — comments welcome on embedded draft sections]
